description: Build the SCP relay-based DID resolution layer (Layer 1, §3.10.2), the primary layer of the dual-layer resolution architecture (§3.10) alongside the existing Mainline DHT fallback (Layer 2). This is issue #482 — a FEATURE, NOT ADR-062 dev-backend cleanup. ADR-062's Slice 11 (SCP-CAPINJECT-011) only severs the InMemoryRelayPublisher default type param; this PRD builds the actual capability. Model B (spec commit aa0722f2b): DID documents ride in a minimal fixed-layout DID-record relay frame (§9.10.12 `DidRecordV1`: version‖public_key‖seq‖signature‖value) carried as a RAW relay blob over the EXISTING PUBLISH/QUERY operations (ADR-004) — no new wire types. Trust is client-side: the resolver re-verifies every record's BEP44 signature against the key derived from the DID string itself (§9.6.1), never the frame-supplied public_key or the relay's acceptance. An SCP-native relay MAY OPTIONALLY validate each frame it stores (decode → DID→routing_id binding → BEP44 signature, cheapest-first) and keep a single highest-sequence slot per routing_id (slot-exclusivity), which delivers the §3.10.8 suppression resistance; foreign/non-validating transports store the frame opaquely and stay correct via client-side verification, the DHT, and multi-relay publishing. Eight stories: 001 the DidRecordV1 frame primitive (scp-protocol, wasm-safe, byte-deterministic); 002 the READ path (transport publish_raw/query_raw + TransportRelayQuerier + completing/correcting the #2226 RealMultiRelayQuerier composer to highest-seq-valid selection without dropping the genuine blob); 003 relay-side validation + slot-exclusivity (with the companion ADR-004 storage-semantics update the spec mandates); 004 the WRITE path (real RelayPublisher + production RepublishManager wiring + the republish-loop signature/sequence-drop fix, republish.rs:703); 005 the publish→resolve round-trip + slot-exclusivity/flood regression tests; 006 the RELAY-CLIENT BINDING — the seam BOTH halves were silently waiting on (the merged TransportRelayQuerier had zero production construction sites and the TransportRelayPublisher was constructed with nothing bound, so neither half was reachable in production; the shipped code justified this with a comment claiming "#482 owns the relay-client binding end to end. No separate issue tracks it", but #482 IS this PRD and no story covered it — phantom provenance, now corrected by 006); 007 the EXTERNAL/BOOTSTRAP relay set (NodeConfig has no relay-URL field and the §18.5.1 five-level chain in DefaultRelayResolver/FALLBACK_RELAYS has zero production callers); 008 the §3.10.5 step 3a relay PUBLISH at DID create/update, which no story in any PRD owned — 004 owns the republish cycle (step 4) only, and the BEP44 signed record is currently discarded by the signing step and read back off the DHT, which is why a DhtMode::Disabled node is fully dormant. Gate numbering is declaration order, not execution order: the DAG is 001 → 002 → {003, 004}, 004 → 006 → {007, 008}, {003, 008} → 005. #2226 (RealMultiRelayQuerier composer) is already merged on main and RETAINED — #482 completes and corrects it, it does not delete it. Pre-rotation/create-ceremony production activation is a SEPARATE dependency (RFC #2130 / #1729) and is NOT required here. Forward-only DAG.

stories.title: Implement the DidRecordV1 DID-record relay frame (version‖public_key‖seq‖signature‖value) in scp-protocol — wasm-safe, byte-deterministic encode/decode with the §9.10.12 decoder-determinism rules
stories.description: Foundational shared primitive for the whole relay-resolution feature (#482). Implement the minimal, fixed-layout DID-record relay frame `DidRecordV1` as a pure sync wasm-compatible type in scp-protocol (§3.10.12 places it in scp-protocol as a Phase-2 type; §9.10.12 is the authoritative frame spec). Layout (§9.10.12): `version: u8 = 1` ‖ `public_key: [u8;32]` (Ed25519, carried for the RELAY's verify; the client ignores it for trust) ‖ `seq: u64` (8 bytes big-endian, BEP44 sequence) ‖ `signature: [u8;64]` (raw fixed-width BEP44 signature, NO length prefix) ‖ `value: [u8]` (the sole variable-length field, the trailing remainder — the BEP44-signed DID-document payload; NO value_len prefix). Fixed prefix = 1+32+8+64 = 105 bytes; total frame length = 105 + len(value). Raw fixed-layout binary encoding under §9.5.1 length-prefix discipline — NOT MessagePack/CBOR/bencode — so the bytes are byte-reproducible across every binding and the exact `value` bytes handed to BEP44 verification are preserved octet-for-octet (§9.10.12 'Why raw binary'). There is deliberately no magic tag and no record-kind byte (the routing-ID domain is the type discriminant, §3.10.2). The frame carries ONLY the (public_key, seq, signature, value) tuple; BEP44 verification is a SEPARATE concern performed by the resolver against the DID-derived key (decode is not verify — §9.10.12 'decode-and-verify at exactly one site' means downstream consumers pair this decode with the single verify site; this type provides the decode). Provides `encode(&self) -> Vec<u8>` and `decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<DidRecordV1, _>`.
acceptanceCriteria: The DidRecordV1 type exists in scp-protocol's envelope module with encode + decode: `grep -rn 'struct DidRecordV1' crates/scp-protocol/src/envelope` matches, and the type exposes an `encode` (-> `Vec<u8>`) and a `decode` (`&[u8]` -> `Result`) function (grep both fn signatures); it is re-exported from `crates/scp-protocol/src/envelope/mod.rs`.

Byte-exact layout: a test asserts `encode` of a fixed (public_key, seq, signature, value) tuple yields exactly `105 + value.len()` bytes, with byte[0] == 0x01 (version), public_key at bytes[1..33], `seq` big-endian at bytes[33..41], signature at bytes[41..105], and value at bytes[105..].

Round-trip determinism: a test encodes a (public_key, seq, signature, value) tuple, decodes the bytes, and asserts the decoded tuple is byte-identical to the input; encoding the decoded value again yields identical bytes (idempotent).

Decoder rule 1 — version gated first: `decode` rejects (returns Err, no partial parse) any frame whose first byte is not 0x01 (an unimplemented version), asserted before any subsequent byte is interpreted; a test feeds a buffer whose first byte is a MessagePack map marker (0x80) and asserts Err (an OuterEnvelope is never mistaken for a frame, §9.10.12).

Decoder rule 2 — full fixed prefix required: `decode` rejects any frame shorter than the 105-byte fixed prefix (a test feeds buffers of length 0, 1, and 104 and asserts Err with no panic in a debug build — proving no `len - 105` underflow, §9.10.12 rule 3).

Decoder rule 3 — value bounds after prefix check: `decode` rejects an empty value (total length exactly 105) and rejects `len(value) > 262144 - 105` (Max blob size 262144, §9.18.11); a test asserts both boundaries (105 rejected; 262039-byte value accepted; 262040-byte value rejected).

wasm-safe / pure sync: the frame type introduces no async or tokio dependency — `grep -n 'tokio\|async ' crates/scp-protocol/src/envelope/did_record.rs` returns 0 (scp-protocol is the wasm32-compatible pure-sync crate, §3.10.12).

Full CI green: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo clippy -p scp-protocol --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$(python3.12 -c "import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_config_var('LIBDIR'))") cargo test -p scp-protocol` — all exit 0.
`python3.12 scripts/validate-prd.py` exits 0 with this story present.
actionItems: Create crates/scp-protocol/src/envelope/did_record.rs with the DidRecordV1 struct (public_key, seq, signature, value) + encode/decode; register `pub mod did_record` and re-export DidRecordV1 in crates/scp-protocol/src/envelope/mod.rs.
Implement encode as fixed-width big-endian writes (version, public_key, seq, signature) followed by the value remainder — no length prefixes on fixed fields, no value_len prefix.

Implement decode enforcing the four §9.10.12 decoder-determinism rules in order: read+check version first; require the full 105-byte prefix; bound-check value length only after the prefix check (reject empty, reject > 262144-105); return the (public_key, seq, signature, value) tuple with no verification.
Write the layout, round-trip, and decoder-determinism (version/prefix/value-bounds/OuterEnvelope-marker) tests; run full CI + review roster.

stories.title: Relay-side validation + slot-exclusivity for DID-record frames (SCP-native relay, OPTIONAL capability): decode → DID→routing_id binding → BEP44 signature (cheapest-first) → single highest-seq slot; slot-exclusive routing_id once claimed — with the companion ADR-004 storage-semantics update the spec mandates
stories.description: The relay-side anti-suppression behavior that makes the relay layer suppression-resistant (§3.10.2 'Relay-side validation', §3.10.8, §9.10.12). This is an OPTIONAL capability of SCP-native relays — the protocol MUST NOT require a validating relay; foreign/non-validating transports store the frame opaquely and stay correct via client-side verification (§3.10.2). On PUBLISH of a blob at a routing_id, a validating SCP-native relay runs, CHEAPEST-FIRST (so junk is rejected before any Ed25519 verify, all behind the existing per-IP PUBLISH rate limit, ADR-004): (1) structural decode as a DidRecordV1 frame (SCP-RELAYRES-001); (2) DID→routing_id binding: confirm `SHA-256("scp:did:" || did(public_key)) == routing_id` where `did(public_key)` is the did:dht string derived from the frame's public_key (§9.6.1) — a plain hash, cheaper than a signature verify, so it runs BEFORE step 3; this mirrors the exact check BRIDGE_REGISTER already performs on the control plane (§10.12.4); (3) BEP44 signature verify over bencode(seq, value) against the frame's public_key, only for a blob that passed 1-2; (4) single highest-sequence slot per routing_id: reject a frame whose seq <= the stored slot's seq UNLESS an equal-seq frame is byte-identical (idempotent TTL refresh), replace only on strictly-higher valid seq. SLOT-EXCLUSIVITY: once a binding-valid, signature-valid frame first establishes a slot at a routing_id, that routing_id becomes slot-exclusive — (a) reject any later PUBLISH there that is not a binding-valid, seq-advancing frame; (b) evict any pre-existing opaque blobs at that routing_id when the slot is first established; (c) QUERY there returns only the single slot. Before the first valid frame the relay cannot recognize the routing_id as DID-domain (SHA-256 is one-way), so pre-seeded junk sits as ordinary opaque blobs until the first valid publish evicts it (§3.10.2/§9.10.12). This is an availability/anti-suppression measure, NEVER a trust dependency — the client re-verifies every record independently, so a relay that skips/botches/lies about validation degrades availability only, never integrity (§3.10.2 'Client always re-verifies'). COMPANION ADR-004 UPDATE (upstream dependency the spec mandates): slot-exclusivity is a relay STORAGE behavior — the base relay stores multiple opaque blobs per routing_id with no per-routing_id cap (ADR-004) — so ADR-004 (§ADR-004: SCP Native Relay Protocol, .docs/adrs/phase-1.md) MUST be updated to specify that DID-domain routing_ids are slot-exclusive once claimed. Per the artifact flow (specs govern ADRs; §3.10.2 is authoritative for the behavior and says 'ADR-004 must be updated to match before the relay implements it'), the ADR-004 update is the FIRST step of this story, before the relay code.
acceptanceCriteria: Companion ADR-004 update landed FIRST: `.docs/adrs/phase-1.md` ADR-004 section documents that DID-domain routing_ids (`SHA-256("scp:did:" || did_string)`) are slot-exclusive once a binding-valid frame establishes a slot — `grep -n 'slot-exclusive\|slot exclusiv' .docs/adrs/phase-1.md` matches within the ADR-004 section (per §3.10.2 mandate).

Validation runs cheapest-first (decode → binding → signature → slot): the validating-relay path decodes the DidRecordV1 frame, then checks the `SHA-256("scp:did:" || did(public_key)) == routing_id` binding, then verifies the BEP44 signature over bencode(seq, value) against the frame's public_key, in that order — a test asserts a wrong-binding frame is rejected WITHOUT an Ed25519 verify being performed (binding check precedes signature, §3.10.2 step 2/3).

Single highest-seq slot: a test asserts a frame with seq <= the stored slot's seq is rejected (unless byte-identical at equal seq = idempotent refresh) and the slot is replaced only on a strictly-higher valid seq (§3.10.2 step 4).

Slot-exclusivity rule (a): once a slot exists at a routing_id, a subsequent PUBLISH that is a non-frame blob, a wrong-binding frame, an invalid signature, or a non-superseding seq is rejected — a test asserts each of the four is rejected once the slot is established (§3.10.2/§3.10.8 flood variants).

Slot-exclusivity rule (b) — pre-seeded eviction: a test pre-seeds opaque junk blobs at a routing_id BEFORE any valid frame, then PUBLISHes the first binding-valid frame, and asserts the pre-existing opaque blobs are evicted when the slot is established (§3.10.2, closing the pre-seeding gap).

Slot-exclusivity rule (c) — QUERY returns only the slot: after a slot is established, a test asserts QUERY at that routing_id returns exactly the single slot record regardless of `limit`, and never any co-located junk.

Validation is OPTIONAL and never a trust dependency: a test asserts a non-validating storage path (foreign/opaque) still accepts and returns the frame as an opaque blob (resolution stays correct via client re-verification), and that relay acceptance is never consumed as a client trust input (the resolver re-verifies) — §3.10.2 'Relay-side validation is an OPTIONAL capability'.

Full CI green: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; the workspace clippy command; `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$(python3.12 -c "import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_config_var('LIBDIR'))") cargo test --workspace` — all exit 0.
`python3.12 scripts/validate-prd.py` exits 0 with this story present.

stories.title: Relay WRITE path (§3.10.5 step 4): a real TransportRelayPublisher that PUBLISHes the DidRecordV1 frame, an UNCONDITIONALLY-scheduled self-healing relay republish arm, and the single-writer live published-state seam the write path required (DidMethod::publish returns the signed record; one shared routing-ID derivation)
stories.description:
The WRITE-path MACHINERY for relay resolution (§3.10.5 step 4) — NOT relay reachability. Read the scope boundary first: this story builds the publisher, fixes the republish loop, constructs the production `RepublishManager`, and fixes the root-cause defects in the node's publish path that the write path structurally depends on. It does NOT make DID records reach relays, because nothing in it establishes a relay-CLIENT connection to bind onto the publisher. That binding is SCP-RELAYRES-006, for which this story is a prerequisite and which delivers the end-to-end reachability. An earlier revision of this description claimed the story wired the manager "so a node actually publishes its own DID document to relays" and was "the story that makes DID records reach relays at all" — that claim was FALSE and is retracted: with zero bound relays every relay publish fails closed (`IdentityError::RelayPublishFailed`). 

REJECTED DESIGN — the one-shot relay latch. An interim revision of this story (and the code it governed) gated the relay arm on a `bound_relay_count()` readiness sample taken ONCE at `RepublishManager` construction, and called `RepublishConfig::disable_relay()` when the sample was zero. That was unfixable by construction: the sample necessarily ran before any relay-client connection could exist, so the arm could never be true and — being latched off — could never be woken. A later revision proposed re-evaluating the sample on every relay tick; that is ALSO rejected, because it keeps a readiness gate the arm does not need. Both are superseded by the shipped design below. No accessor named `bound_relay_count` exists in the shipped code, and no scheduling decision reads a relay count. 

SHIPPED DESIGN — schedule unconditionally, fail closed per tick, self-heal. The relay arm is scheduled whenever the node has a published signed record, with NO readiness sample of any kind. `TransportRelayPublisher::publish` fails closed with a typed `IdentityError::RelayPublishFailed` while no relay is bound; `relay_republish_loop` treats that as a failure and backs off 30s doubling to a 30-minute cap, so an unbound relay costs at most one no-op wakeup per 30 minutes, and fires `RelayPublishDegraded` through the warning callback once consecutive total failures reach `DEGRADED_THRESHOLD`. A relay bound LATER — by SCP-RELAYRES-006, on the same shared publisher instance — self-heals the arm on its next tick, with no manager reconstruction and no re-drive. `RepublishConfig::disable_relay()` is reserved for a DELIBERATE user opt-out (§3.10.6, which mandates a warning); an unbound layer is not one, so the production path MUST NOT call it and no §3.10.6 layer-disabled warning is emitted while merely unbound. 

This story delivers: (a) a real production `RelayPublisher` in scp-transport that encodes an already-validated `DidRecordV1` (SCP-RELAYRES-001) and PUBLISHes the frame bytes at the DID routing_id via the `publish_raw` transport path (SCP-RELAYRES-002) — the DID relay blob MUST be the DidRecordV1 frame, not the bare document bytes and not an OuterEnvelope (§9.10.12 publish contract) — fanning out to every bound relay, reporting `RelayPublishOutcome { accepted, attempted }` so a PARTIAL accept is surfaced as §3.10.8 suppression rather than counted as success, and failing closed when zero relays accept; (b) the relay-republish loop building and publishing the full frame from the `RepublishEntry`'s (public_key, signature, sequence, document_bytes), so signature and sequence are no longer dropped; (c) the production `RepublishManager` at the node/self-host construction site (crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs), adding the 6-day relay republish cycle (blob_ttl 7 days, 1-day margin, §3.10.2/§3.10.5) alongside the existing 2-hour DHT cycle, both arms always enabled (§3.10.6 anti-segmentation — the relay cycle is additive, never a replacement). 

ROOT-CAUSE FIXES the write path required (all shipped in this story, not a separate one — see `details.scopeException`). The write path cannot publish a frame it cannot build, and cannot keep publishing the right frame if its source is a build-time snapshot: (d) `DidMethod::publish` returns the signed BEP44 record it already computed instead of `()`, so the (public_key, seq, signature, value) triple is an OUTPUT of signing and re-deriving it by resolving the node's own record back off the DHT is structurally impossible — the read-back made republishing depend on a remote read succeeding, pinned whatever a responder returned, and froze at the first read so an in-lifetime rotation was never re-seeded; (e) the node's published state — the signed record, the DID document the dev API serves, and the relay URL `.well-known/scp` advertises — is read from LIVE slots rather than build-time snapshots, with a single object-safe publish seam as the only production writer, so a NAT tier change (§10.12.1 "Tier changes are transparent — the DID document is updated with the new relay address") re-points every consumer instead of leaving the DHT arm re-putting a superseded `seq` (which BEP44 nodes reject) and the relay arm pushing a superseded frame (which a validating relay rejects, miscounted as a publish failure); the tier-change endpoint is routed through that same seam rather than publishing around it; (f) `HealingPublisher::heal` takes an indivisible `&DidRecordV1` rather than four loose positional fields, so §3.10.7 protocol-level healing cannot silently reorder or mix them, and a framing failure is the typed `IdentityError::DidRecordFramingFailed`; (g) the DID routing-ID derivations are defined exactly once and shared by all three consumers — the relay WRITE path, relay DID-record ADMISSION, and `BRIDGE_REGISTER` — so the write path and the admission check cannot drift (§10.12.4.1 forbids conflating derivations). 

The InMemoryRelayPublisher default was already severed and demoted to test-harness-only by SCP-CAPINJECT-011 (cross-PRD dependency); this story supplies the real `R` the severed API now requires, and is the first production `RepublishManager` construction site to exist — which supersedes that story's AC4 (see the CAPINJECT PRD `details`). Relay PUBLISH at DID create/update (§3.10.5 step 3a) is SCP-RELAYRES-008, not this story: this story owns the REPUBLISH cycle only.
acceptanceCriteria: Real production RelayPublisher in scp-transport: `grep -rn 'impl RelayPublisher for' crates/scp-transport/src` matches a real (non-InMemory, non-test) publisher; it encodes the already-validated frame itself and publishes the ENCODED bytes — `grep -n 'record.encode()' crates/scp-transport/src/native/relay_publisher.rs` matches and `grep -n 'record.value()' crates/scp-transport/src/native/relay_publisher.rs` returns 0 (never the bare document bytes, §9.10.12) — addresses the blob via the shared `did_record_routing_id` derivation, and calls `publish_raw`; the module is registered in native/mod.rs. A test asserts the published blob decodes and is admitted by the relay-side DID-record validation path (`published_frame_is_admitted_by_relay_validation`).

Republish loop publishes the full frame (signature/sequence no longer dropped): a test drives the relay-republish path with a recording publisher and asserts the published blob decodes via `DidRecordV1::decode` into the SAME (public_key, signature, seq) and value=document_bytes as the source `RepublishEntry` (`relay_republish_publishes_full_frame_not_bare_document_bytes`, crates/scp-identity/src/republish.rs); an entry that cannot be framed fails closed with the relay arm disabled for that identity rather than publishing something else (`relay_republish_fails_closed_on_unframeable_entry`).

The relay arm is scheduled UNCONDITIONALLY and self-heals — no readiness sample, no latch: crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs constructs the `RepublishManager` naming the real scp-transport `TransportRelayPublisher` as its `R` type parameter (grep the construction); the relay republish interval is the 6-day cycle (518400s, §3.10.2/§3.10.5, asserted by `relay_default_republish_interval_is_six_days`); `grep -n 'disable_relay' crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs` returns 0 matches — the production path never disables the relay arm; and `grep -rn 'bound_relay_count' crates/scp-identity/src/republish.rs crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs` returns 0 — no scheduling decision reads a relay count. A test starts the production `start_self_did_republishing` entry point with ZERO relays bound, asserts the relay arm IS scheduled anyway (`active_relay_count().await == 1`), binds a relay on the SAME shared publisher instance afterwards, advances past the first backoff, and asserts the next tick publishes a decodable DidRecordV1 frame with no manager reconstruction and no re-drive (`relay_arm_self_heals_when_a_relay_is_bound_after_start`, crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs).

Zero bound relays fails closed and backs off — never a phantom success, never a silent opt-out: with no relay bound `TransportRelayPublisher::publish` returns `IdentityError::RelayPublishFailed` and not `Ok` (`unbound_publisher_fails_closed`), and every bound relay rejecting is likewise `Err` (`all_relays_fail_is_fail_closed`) — zero accepts is never an `Ok` outcome; `relay_republish_loop` sleeps `backoff_secs(consecutive_failures - 1)`, 30s doubling to a 30-minute cap (`INITIAL_BACKOFF_SECS = 30`, `MAX_BACKOFF_SECS = 30 * 60`, asserted by `backoff_sequence_is_correct`), so an unbound relay costs at most one no-op wakeup per 30 minutes rather than one per 6-day cycle; the degraded callback fires once consecutive total failures reach `DEGRADED_THRESHOLD` (`relay_warning_callback_fires_after_degraded_threshold`); and the §3.10.6 layer-disabled warning callback is wired but NOT fired by an unbound layer (`self_host_republish_config_wires_the_layer_disabled_warning`) — an unbound layer is not a user opt-out. End-to-end production reachability — a relay bound by PRODUCTION code with a frame landing in its blob store — is asserted by SCP-RELAYRES-006; this story structurally cannot satisfy it and does not claim to.

Both-layer publish preserved (§3.10.6): a test drives the production `start_self_did_republishing` with a signed record present and asserts BOTH arms are scheduled — the existing DHT 2-hour cycle AND the relay 6-day cycle — with neither arm disabled by the production path (`self_did_republishing_schedules_both_dht_and_relay_layers`, `production_republish_manager_publishes_both_layers`). With no published record the manager is fully dormant at ZERO arms rather than scheduling arms with nothing to keep alive (`self_did_republishing_fully_dormant_without_published_record`).

`DidMethod::publish` returns the signed record, so a network read-back is structurally impossible: `grep -n 'fn publish' -A 5 crates/scp-identity/src/lib.rs` shows the trait method returning `Result<republish::RepublishEntry, IdentityError>` and never `Result<(), _>`; `DidDht::publish_document` returns the (public_key, seq, signature, value) it already computed (grep crates/scp-identity/src/dht.rs for the `RepublishEntry` construction at the end of the publish body); `grep -n 'self_did_republish_entry' crates/` returns 0 and `grep -n 'dht_client.resolve' crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs` returns 0 — the node never resolves its own record back off the network to rebuild the triple. A test asserts republishing still starts when the DHT holds NO record for this node, the exact shape a resolve timeout takes (`republishing_survives_a_dht_read_back_miss_at_startup`, crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs).

Single-writer LIVE published state (no frozen snapshot), enforced by construction: the node's published state — the signed record the republish arms keep alive, the DID document the dev API serves, and the relay URL `.well-known/scp` advertises — lives in live slots read per call, never captured by value at build time. The slot's mutating accessor is visible ONLY inside the private module that also holds the node's single post-construction writer, so an out-of-band write from elsewhere in `scp-node` is a COMPILE ERROR rather than a convention (grep the module for the non-`pub(crate)` mutator). Every publish of this node's DID document — startup and tier change alike — goes through one object-safe publish seam, `DidPublisher`, whose only production impl (`NodeDidPublisher`) binds the configured `DhtMode` gate so no path can reach the underlying `DidMethod` around it (`grep -rn 'trait DidPublisher' crates/scp-node/src` matches; `publish_did_document_for_mode` has exactly one non-test caller), and the tier-change function takes that seam as a parameter. NOTE — the seam no longer performs the publish and the slot write in ONE expression: collapsing the three slots into a single `NodePublishedState` made the slot unconstructible before the startup publish that produces its `record`, so the write moved out of `NodeDidPublisher` and into the three call sites. All three do write it, but 'a caller cannot publish without re-seeding' is now a property of those call sites rather than of the type. See `details.weakened_by_collapse` (`grep -rn 'trait DidPublisher' crates/scp-node/src` matches, and the tier-change function takes the seam as a parameter). `start_self_did_republishing` takes a `tokio::sync::watch` receiver over the published-record slot, never a `RepublishEntry` by value (grep its signature in crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs). Tests drive a NAT tier change through the production path and assert each live consumer observes the NEW value: `tier_change_reseeds_the_running_republish_arms` (both arms re-seed to the new (value, signature, seq) instead of re-putting the superseded record), `tier_change_advances_every_advertised_surface_in_agreement` and `tier_change_advances_every_surface_on_a_node_that_publishes_nothing` (each asserts the dev-API document, the `IdentityHandle` document, the `.well-known` top-level `relay`, the invite-URI `relay=` parameters and `relay_url()` have ALL advanced and ALL AGREE — the four earlier per-surface tests pinned no surface to any other), `a_failed_republish_advances_the_address_but_not_the_document`, `tier_change_appends_a_relay_service_when_the_document_carries_none`, `tier_change_repoints_only_the_preferred_relay_entry`, and `the_nodes_own_relay_entry_is_installed_at_the_preferred_position` (§10.12.1 "Tier changes are transparent — the DID document is updated with the new relay address").

§3.10.7 protocol-level healing takes an indivisible frame, so bare bytes are unrepresentable: `grep -n 'fn heal' -A 4 crates/scp-identity/src/resolver.rs` shows `HealingPublisher::heal` taking `&DidRecordV1` and NOT four loose (public_key, seq, signature, value) parameters that a caller could reorder or mix; a `DidRecordV1` is constructible only through the validating `DidRecordV1::try_new`; and a frame that cannot be built is the typed `IdentityError::DidRecordFramingFailed` (grep the variant in crates/scp-identity/src/lib.rs and its construction in resolver.rs) rather than a silent skip.

ONE routing-ID derivation per domain, shared by every consumer (§10.12.4.1 — implementations MUST NOT conflate the derivation schemes): `grep -rn 'fn did_key_routing_id\|fn did_record_routing_id' crates/` matches ONLY crates/scp-identity/src/resolution.rs, and both are re-exported from the crate root (grep crates/scp-identity/src/lib.rs). All three consumers call the shared helpers instead of re-deriving inline: the relay WRITE path (crates/scp-transport/src/native/relay_publisher.rs calls `did_record_routing_id`), relay DID-record ADMISSION (crates/scp-transport/src/relay/did_record_validation.rs calls `did_record_routing_id`), and `BRIDGE_REGISTER` (crates/scp-transport/src/relay/bridge.rs calls `did_key_routing_id`) — grep each call site. The admission and bridge tests recompute the hash independently rather than calling the shared helper, so a bug in the helper cannot be masked by the test that exercises it.

`RelayPublisher::publish` takes the TTL plus an already-validated frame and reports fan-out honestly: `grep -n 'fn publish' -A 5 crates/scp-identity/src/republish.rs` shows `publish(&self, blob_ttl_secs: u64, record: &DidRecordV1) -> impl Future<Output = Result<RelayPublishOutcome, IdentityError>>`; a publish fans out to EVERY bound relay rather than the first (`publishes_to_all_bound_relays`); one relay failing while another accepts is `Ok` with `accepted < attempted` (`one_relay_fails_other_succeeds_is_success`); and the republish loop treats that partial accept as §3.10.8 suppression — firing `RelayPublishDegraded` on the FIRST occurrence, not after the threshold, and sleeping the normal interval rather than backing off onto the healthy relays (`partial_relay_accept_fires_degraded_callback_immediately`), while a complete accept fires no callback (`complete_relay_accept_fires_no_degraded_callback`).

actionItems: Create crates/scp-transport/src/native/relay_publisher.rs implementing the scp-identity `RelayPublisher` trait over a shared `BoundRelays` map: encode the `DidRecordV1`, address it via the shared `did_record_routing_id`, PUBLISH the frame bytes to every bound relay via `publish_raw`, return `RelayPublishOutcome { accepted, attempted }`, and fail closed with `IdentityError::RelayPublishFailed` when nothing is bound or every bound relay rejects; register the module in native/mod.rs.

Fix the crates/scp-identity/src/republish.rs relay-republish loop to build a `DidRecordV1` frame from the `RepublishEntry` (public_key, signature, sequence, document_bytes) and publish the frame — stop publishing bare document_bytes — and surface a partial accept as the §3.10.8 suppression warning plus an immediate `RelayPublishDegraded`.

Wire the production `RepublishManager<Dht, TransportRelayPublisher>` at crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs with the real relay publisher and the 6-day relay republish cycle alongside the 2-hour DHT cycle. Schedule the relay arm UNCONDITIONALLY whenever a signed record exists — no readiness sample at construction and no per-tick relay-count check; let the publisher fail closed per tick and the loop's 30s→30min backoff absorb the unbound window, so a later bind self-heals the arm. Do NOT call `RepublishConfig::disable_relay()` on any production path (§3.10.6 reserves it for a deliberate user opt-out, which an unbound layer is not).

Change `DidMethod::publish` to return the `RepublishEntry` it already signs, update `DidDht::publish_document` and every `impl DidMethod` in the workspace, and delete the self-DID DHT read-back that reconstructed the triple by resolving the node's own record.

Replace the node's build-time snapshots of published state (signed record, DID document, relay URL) with ONE live slot type in a private module whose mutating accessor is not visible outside it, put the node's single post-construction writer (the tier-change path) in that module beside it, and route every startup publish through one object-safe publish seam that writes the slot in the same expression as the publish. Hand the republish cycle a `watch::Receiver` over the record slot instead of an entry by value, and propagate the by-value `relay_url()` through the node, HTTP/dev/well-known surfaces and all four FFI server wrappers so no consumer can hold a stale copy.

Change `HealingPublisher::heal` to take `&DidRecordV1` and add the typed `IdentityError::DidRecordFramingFailed`; move the `did_key_routing_id` / `did_record_routing_id` pair into crates/scp-identity/src/resolution.rs as the single definition, re-export both symmetrically from the crate root, and repoint the WRITE path, the relay DID-record admission check, and `BRIDGE_REGISTER` at the shared helpers.

Write the frame-encode/admission, republish-full-frame, unconditional-scheduling + self-heal, fail-closed + backoff + degraded, both-layer-scheduled, read-back-miss, tier-change re-seed (all four live consumers), and fan-out/partial-accept tests; run full CI + review roster.

details.does_not_deliver: relay reachability. No relay-client connection is established by this story, so with zero bound relays every relay publish fails closed. SCP-RELAYRES-006 delivers the binding; SCP-RELAYRES-007 the external/bootstrap relay set; SCP-RELAYRES-008 the create/update relay leg.
details.retracted_claim: The prior description's "This is the story that makes DID records reach relays at all" was phantom provenance and is retracted (the shipped code justified the dead relay arm with a comment claiming "#482 owns the relay-client binding end to end. No separate issue tracks it" — #482 IS this PRD, which had no such story until SCP-RELAYRES-006).
details.rejected_design: The one-shot relay latch: gating the relay arm on a `bound_relay_count()` readiness sample taken once at `RepublishManager` construction and calling `RepublishConfig::disable_relay()` when it read zero. Unfixable by construction — the sample necessarily ran before any relay client could exist, so the arm could never be true and, being latched, could never be woken. The per-tick re-evaluation variant an interim revision of this story proposed is ALSO rejected: it retains a readiness gate the arm does not need. Superseded by unconditional scheduling + fail-closed-per-tick + backoff + self-heal. No `bound_relay_count` accessor exists in the shipped code, and no scheduling decision reads a relay count.
details.scopeException: This story spans 23 files rather than the ~3 the PRD standard prefers, because the relay WRITE path and its root-cause fixes are one atomic unit: the publisher cannot build a frame the signing step discards (`DidMethod::publish` returning the record), and the republish arms cannot keep publishing the CURRENT frame from a build-time snapshot (the live published-state slots + single publish seam). Splitting them retroactively would invent a sequencing that never existed and leave stories that are done-on-arrival with a backwards dependency. Everything the branch built is owned by an acceptance criterion here; nothing is left justified only by rustdoc.
details.weakened_by_collapse: The live-slot collapse (one `LiveSlot<NodePublishedState>` replacing `NodeDidDocument` + `NodeRelayUrl` + `PublishedDidRecord`) removed a compile-time guarantee its predecessor had. `NodeDidPublisher` used to OWN the `PublishedDidRecord` slot as a required field and write it inside `publish`, so publishing without re-seeding was not constructible; its own comment called splitting them 'exactly the frozen-snapshot defect this seam exists to make unrepresentable'. The unified `NodePublishedState` needs document + relay_url + record together, so it cannot exist before the startup publish that produces the record — which forced the write out to the callers. No live defect: all three production publish sites (`build_domain_inner`, `build_no_domain_inner`, `apply_tier_change`) do store the record. But the guarantee is now conventional, not structural. Restoring it means moving the trait, `NodeDidPublisher` and the startup publish-and-seed into the private `published_state` module so the trait method is unnameable outside it — a real restructure of the seam, and the FIFTH pass over it, so it is escalated rather than folded in silently.

stories.title: End-to-end relay-only publish→resolve round-trip + dual-layer suppression-resilience and slot-exclusivity/flood regression tests, including a DhtMode::Disabled node resolving its own and a peer's DID via the relay
stories.description: Integration coverage proving the READ + WRITE halves interoperate and the relay layer delivers the §3.10.8 suppression resilience it claims. Only both halves together restore that resilience (a real querier reading relays a real publisher actually populates), so this story exercises the full loop across a validating SCP-native relay. Tests: (1) RELAY-ONLY publish→resolve round-trip — publish a DID document ONLY to a relay (not the DHT) via the real RelayPublisher (SCP-RELAYRES-004) and resolve it back via the real TransportRelayQuerier + RealMultiRelayQuerier composer through the DualLayerResolver (SCP-RELAYRES-002), asserting the resolved document is byte-identical and verifies (§3.10.4/§3.10.5); (2) DUAL-LAYER suppression resilience — suppression on one layer is defeated by the other; with the record on a relay and the DHT, dropping either still resolves (§3.10.8); (3) FLOOD inert on a validating relay — junk frame (malformed/wrong-binding/bad-sig), valid-looking frame with stale/equal seq, non-frame opaque junk, and pre-seeded junk are ALL inert against the single highest-seq slot (SCP-RELAYRES-003), and the genuine record still resolves (§3.10.8 four flood variants); (4) DhtMode::Disabled node — a Disabled node (DHT arm off) publishes its OWN DID to a relay and resolves its own DID back via the relay, AND resolves a PEER's DID published to a relay (this completes the A2 self-DID + peer resolution path noted in SCP-CAPINJECT-001 / ADR-062 A2↔A4 sequencing, which relay resolution — this feature — brings online). SEQUENCING (dependency correctness): tests (1)-(3) require a live relay reachable from PRODUCTION code, which is the relay-client binding (SCP-RELAYRES-006), not SCP-RELAYRES-004 — 004 ships the publisher with nothing bound to it. Tests (4)-(5) additionally require SCP-RELAYRES-008, because the node's publish path currently gates BOTH legs on `DhtMode`: `DhtMode::Disabled` — the fail-closed default — returns `Ok(None)` and publishes nothing on either layer, so a Disabled node has no signed record at all, its `RepublishManager` sits fully dormant at zero arms, and it can neither relay-publish its own DID nor be resolved. 008 splits that gating (§3.10.6 treats the layers as independently gated) and adds the §3.10.5 step 3a relay leg, which is what makes AC[3]/AC[4] reachable. NOTE — an earlier revision of this paragraph gave a DIFFERENT and now-FALSE reason: that the BEP44 `(value, signature, seq)` triple was reconstructed by resolving the node's own record back off the DHT via `self_did_republish_entry`. SCP-RELAYRES-004 removed that read-back entirely — `DidMethod::publish` returns the signed record and `grep -n 'self_did_republish_entry' crates/` returns 0 — so do not re-derive a dependency from it. `blockedBy` therefore lists SCP-RELAYRES-003 and SCP-RELAYRES-008; 008 transitively covers 006, which transitively covers 004 and 002 (no transitive over-specification, no cycle).
acceptanceCriteria: Relay-only publish→resolve round-trip: a test publishes a DID document to a relay ONLY (DHT not used) via the real RelayPublisher and resolves it back through the real querier + DualLayerResolver, asserting the resolved document + (value, signature, seq) is byte-identical to the published one and verifies against the DID-derived key (§3.10.4/§3.10.5).

Dual-layer suppression resilience: a test with the record present on both a relay and the DHT asserts resolution still succeeds when the relay layer is suppressed (DHT serves it) and when the DHT layer is suppressed (relay serves it) — §3.10.8; and asserts that when BOTH layers hold nothing the resolver returns honest not-found Ok(None), never a fabricated document (§3.10.4).

Flood inert on a validating relay (four variants): a test asserts that against a validating relay holding the genuine slot, each of a junk frame, a stale/equal-seq frame, a non-frame opaque blob, and pre-seeded junk fails to displace the genuine record, and the genuine record still resolves (§3.10.8).

DhtMode::Disabled self-DID via relay: a test constructs a DhtMode::Disabled node (DHT-layer-off), publishes its OWN DID to a relay via the real RelayPublisher, and asserts it resolves its own DID back via the real querier (self-DID resolution requires the write half — completing SCP-CAPINJECT-001 A2).

DhtMode::Disabled peer-DID via relay: the same test (or a sibling) asserts the Disabled node resolves a PEER's DID that was published to a relay — confirming the ADR-062 A2↔A4 sequencing note that a Disabled node's peer resolution comes online with relay resolution (§3.10.2/§3.10.4).

`python3.12 scripts/validate-prd.py` exits 0 with this story present.

Exercise the full stack: real RelayPublisher (004) -> validating relay + slot-exclusivity (003) -> TransportRelayQuerier + composer (002) -> DualLayerResolver, using DidRecordV1 (001) end to end.

stories.title: Relay-client binding: share ONE live relay connection across the READ and WRITE halves — add the `Arc<dyn TransportAdapter>` blanket impl, bind the self-host node's own loopback relay onto both TransportRelayQuerier and TransportRelayPublisher, and replace NoOpRelayQuerier with the bound RealMultiRelayQuerier in the node's production DualLayerResolver
stories.description:
THE MISSING SEAM. Both halves of relay resolution ship a type that holds a late-bound `relay_url -> Arc<dyn TransportAdapter>` map, and NEITHER has a production `bind` caller: `TransportRelayQuerier` (SCP-RELAYRES-002, merged) has ZERO production construction sites of any kind — production DID resolution still runs `NoOpRelayQuerier` (crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs `build_shared_cache_key_resolver`) — and `TransportRelayPublisher` (SCP-RELAYRES-004) is constructed on the serve path with nothing ever bound, so every relay publish fails closed on every tick. The two halves await the SAME thing: one relay-client connection set. No artifact owned that work — the shipped code justified the dead relay arm with a comment claiming "#482 owns the relay-client binding end to end. No separate issue tracks it", but #482 IS this PRD and this PRD had no such story. That is phantom provenance; THIS story is the artifact the code descends from. SCOPE — the node's OWN relay only (§18.5.2 agent-deployment case: "The agent's relay is self-hosted — no external relay discovery needed"). The self-host node already opens exactly one live relay-client connection to its own relay: `connect_loopback_supervisor` (crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs) builds a `NativeRelayAdapter` for `ws://127.0.0.1:{relay_port}/scp/v1` and moves it BY VALUE into `RelayTransportProvider::new`, so no second reference survives to bind. That is the whole mechanical friction, and it is ~5 lines of trait plumbing: crates/scp-transport/src/traits.rs has a blanket `impl TransportAdapter for Box<dyn TransportAdapter>` but no `Arc` counterpart. Adding `impl TransportAdapter for Arc<dyn TransportAdapter>` (mechanical forwarding of the eight trait methods, mirroring the existing Box impl) lets ONE `Arc<dyn TransportAdapter>` be cloned into the supervisor's transport provider AND bound onto both the querier and the publisher — one socket, three consumers, no second connection. This story: (1) add the `Arc<dyn TransportAdapter>` blanket impl; (2) construct the loopback adapter once as `Arc<dyn TransportAdapter>` and bind it, under its relay URL, onto BOTH the shared `TransportRelayPublisher` (WRITE) and a `TransportRelayQuerier` (READ) — one bind site feeding both halves, because they are the same seam; (3) replace `NoOpRelayQuerier` in the node's production `DualLayerResolver` with `RealMultiRelayQuerier<TransportRelayQuerier>` over the bound querier, and pass the bound relay URL as the resolver's bootstrap-relay list (it is currently `Vec::new()`, so the relay layer is never consulted even in principle); (4) expose the bound-relay count as an OBSERVABILITY-ONLY accessor on `TransportRelayPublisher` and `TransportRelayQuerier` (a public wrapper over the existing `pub(crate) BoundRelays::len()`), so this story and SCP-RELAYRES-007 can assert bind outcomes mechanically. 
BIND ORDERING IS NOT AN INVARIANT — read this before writing any test. The relay arm is scheduled UNCONDITIONALLY and self-heals (SCP-RELAYRES-004): it needs no relay bound at start, so this story does NOT have to bind before `start_self_did_republishing`, and MUST NOT reintroduce an ordering requirement, a readiness sample, or any arm-activation gate keyed on the relay count. The one-shot latch that did exactly that is the REJECTED design (see SCP-RELAYRES-004 `details.rejected_design`); binding earlier only shortens the first backoff window, it does not enable anything. The count accessor added here is for observability and assertions ONLY.

stories.title: External and bootstrap relay set: add the NodeConfig relay-URL field, drive the §18.5.1 five-level bootstrap priority chain through the currently-dead DefaultRelayResolver, and bind every resolved relay onto the shared publisher + querier
stories.description: SCP-RELAYRES-006 binds the ONE relay the self-host node runs itself (§18.5.2). This story adds the relays it does NOT run: the identity's own external relays and the bootstrap/fallback set, which is what §3.10.2 "Multi-relay" requires ("Identity owners SHOULD publish to multiple relays — their own relays plus bootstrap relays from the fallback relay list (§18.5.1) — for availability and suppression resistance") and what §3.10.4 step 3a queries ("identity's published relays if known, else bootstrap relays from §18.5.1"). Two independent gaps make the §18.5.1 chain dead today: (1) `NodeConfig` (crates/scp-node/src/config.rs) has NO relay-URL field — `bind_addr` is the relay SERVER's listen address, not a client relay set — so §18.5.1 level 1 ("Explicit configuration. Relay URLs provided directly in TransportConfig at SDK initialization") is unreachable from the node surface; (2) `DefaultRelayResolver` and `FALLBACK_RELAYS` (crates/scp-transport/src/config.rs) implement all five levels and are unit-tested, and `DefaultRelayResolver`/`ResolveRelays` are re-exported from crates/scp-transport/src/lib.rs — but the resolver is never CONSTRUCTED outside its own unit tests, so no shipped code path ever runs the chain. This story: (a) add an explicit `relay_urls: Vec<String>` field to `NodeConfig`, defaulted to empty by `NodeConfig::defaults` and threaded END-TO-END — explicitly NOT the carried-but-dropped shape `dht_gateways` currently has (that field is documented as "carried but not yet threaded end-to-end" and dropped in `split_config`; repeating it here would ship a config knob that silently does nothing); (b) drive `DefaultRelayResolver` from the node with level 1 = the new field and levels 2-5 wired to their real providers, logging the §18.5.1 warning when the chain falls through to the hardcoded fallback list; (c) open one `NativeRelayAdapter` connection per resolved relay URL and bind each onto the SAME shared `TransportRelayPublisher` and `TransportRelayQuerier` instances SCP-RELAYRES-006 established — one connection set feeding both halves, additively with the loopback binding; (d) pass the full resolved set (loopback + external + bootstrap) as the `DualLayerResolver`'s bootstrap-relay list. A relay that fails to connect is skipped and logged, never bound and never fatal (§3.10.8 "Relay unresponsive, slow, or withholding": a single bad relay must not block resolution or startup). Scope boundary: WHEN a DID record is published (create/update vs the republish cycle) is SCP-RELAYRES-004 (republish) and SCP-RELAYRES-008 (create/update); this story owns WHICH relays receive it.
acceptanceCriteria: `NodeConfig` gains an explicit relay-URL field: `grep -n 'pub relay_urls' crates/scp-node/src/config.rs` matches a `Vec<String>` field, `NodeConfig::defaults` initialises it to an empty vec (grep the initialiser), and the field is threaded end-to-end — a test builds a node with `relay_urls: vec![reachable_url]` and asserts that URL is bound on BOTH the shared publisher and the shared querier after start (it is not dropped in `split_config` the way `dht_gateways` is).

§18.5.1 chain has a production caller: `grep -rn 'DefaultRelayResolver' crates/scp-node/src` matches at least one non-test line; a test asserts level 1 (explicit `relay_urls`) short-circuits levels 2-5 (no DID-document, `.well-known`, or peer lookup is performed when explicit URLs are supplied).

Level-5 fallback warns: a test with no explicit URLs and no level 2-4 provider result asserts the resolver returns the `FALLBACK_RELAYS` entries AND emits the §18.5.1 fallback warning ("The SDK SHOULD warn when falling back to default relays").

Every resolved relay is bound, not just the first: a test with three reachable resolved relay URLs asserts the shared `TransportRelayPublisher`'s observability count accessor (SCP-RELAYRES-006) reports exactly 3, all three URLs are bound on the querier, and a single `RelayPublisher::publish` reaches all three — the returned `RelayPublishOutcome` is `accepted == 3, attempted == 3` and every one of the three recording relays holds the frame (§3.10.2 "Multi-relay", multi-relay publishing for suppression resistance).

Resolver queries the resolved set, not just the loopback: the node's `DualLayerResolver` is constructed with the full resolved relay URL set — a test where a DID's record exists ONLY on an external relay asserts it resolves with `ResolutionSource::ScpRelay { relay_url }` equal to that external relay's URL (§3.10.4 step 3a).

A failing relay is skipped, never phantom-bound, never fatal: a test with one reachable and one unreachable relay URL asserts the node still starts, the observability count accessor reports exactly 1, the unreachable URL has NO binding on either the publisher or the querier, and the connect failure is logged (§3.10.8 — one bad relay cannot block a result from another).

stories.title: §3.10.5 step 3a: add the relay PUBLISH leg at every DID create/update, gate the relay leg INDEPENDENTLY of DhtMode so a Disabled node still relay-publishes (§3.10.6), and rename the DHT-only publish entry point to name both layers
stories.description:
§3.10.5 makes the two publish legs PARALLEL and both a MUST: step 3a wraps `(public_key, seq, signature, value)` in a DID-record frame (§9.10.12) and PUBLISHes it to SCP relays with `blob_ttl: 604800`; step 3b is `DhtClient.publish`. §3.10.6 states the rule outright — "Publishing to both layers is a MUST, not a SHOULD." Only the DHT leg exists today: the node's publish path (`publish_did_document_for_mode`, crates/scp-node/src/lib.rs) calls `DidMethod::publish` and nothing else. No story in this PRD or any other owns step 3a — SCP-RELAYRES-004 owns the REPUBLISH cycle (§3.10.5 step 4), not the create/update publish. 

WHAT IS ALREADY DELIVERED — do NOT re-implement it. An earlier revision of this story asserted a root cause that SCP-RELAYRES-004 has since fixed, and that premise is now FALSE: `DidMethod::publish` no longer returns `Result<(), IdentityError>` discarding the signed record — it returns `republish::RepublishEntry` carrying (public_key, seq, signature, value) (crates/scp-identity/src/lib.rs, built in crates/scp-identity/src/dht.rs), so the triple IS an output of signing and any caller can build the frame; and `self_did_republish_entry` — the function that reconstructed the triple by resolving the node's own record back off the DHT — no longer exists (`grep -n 'self_did_republish_entry' crates/` returns 0, and `grep -n 'dht_client.resolve' crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs` returns 0). Both of that revision's corresponding acceptance criteria are satisfied; they have been removed from this story and recorded in `details.delivered_by_004`. 

WHAT GENUINELY REMAINS is the layer asymmetry and the misnomer that encodes it. The node's publish path is gated ENTIRELY on `DhtMode`: `DhtMode::Disabled` — the fail-closed default — returns `Ok(None)` and publishes nothing on EITHER layer, so a Disabled node has no signed record, its `RepublishManager` sits fully dormant at zero arms, and it is unreachable by relay resolution as well as by the DHT. §3.10.6 treats the two layers as independently gated, so that is wrong twice over: turning the DHT layer off must not turn the relay layer off, and the entry point's name (`publish_did_document_for_mode`) says "for mode" while gating both legs on a DHT-specific mode. This story: (a) SPLIT THE GATING — signing becomes unconditional, the DHT leg stays gated on `DhtMode`, and the relay leg is gated ONLY on the relay layer's own enablement, because a `DhtMode::Disabled` node MUST still relay-publish; (b) ADD THE STEP-3a RELAY LEG — wrap the one signed record in a `DidRecordV1` (SCP-RELAYRES-001) and PUBLISH via the shared `TransportRelayPublisher` (SCP-RELAYRES-004) bound by SCP-RELAYRES-006, `blob_ttl: 604800`, in parallel with the DHT leg and driven from the SAME signing, so both layers receive byte-identical `(value, signature, seq)`; (c) RENAME the entry point so it names both layers rather than the DHT mode. The frame is transport framing and NEVER enters the signed bytes (§3.10.5, §9.10.12 "Framing is outside the signed authority"). 
Once the relay leg is unconditional, a `DhtMode::Disabled` node acquires a signed record for the first time, which is what lifts its `RepublishManager` out of full dormancy and lets the 6-day relay arm run — the structural reason SCP-RELAYRES-005 AC4 ("a DhtMode::Disabled node publishes its OWN DID to a relay and resolves it back") cannot pass today, and the same claim ADR-062's A2↔A4 sequencing note makes. Scope boundary: WHICH relays receive the publish is SCP-RELAYRES-006 (the node's own relay) and SCP-RELAYRES-007 (external + bootstrap); this story owns WHEN (every create/update) and WHAT (the frame built from the one signed record).
acceptanceCriteria: Relay leg exists at create/update and is driven from the SAME signing as the DHT leg: a test drives a DID create through the production node publish path with a bound relay and asserts (i) a blob at the DID routing ID on that relay `DidRecordV1::decode`s, (ii) its `blob_ttl` is 604800, and (iii) its `(value, signature, seq)` is byte-identical to what the DHT leg received — one signing, two layers (§3.10.5 "Both layers receive identical document bytes and identical BEP44 signatures").

The relay leg is NOT gated on `DhtMode`: a test with `DhtMode::Disabled` asserts the DHT publish is skipped AND the relay PUBLISH still happens (§3.10.6 — the layers are independently gated); the `DhtMode::Disabled` arm no longer short-circuits the whole publish function, and a test asserts a Disabled node's create yields a decodable frame on its bound relay.

A `DhtMode::Disabled` node is no longer dormant: a test asserts a Disabled node's create produces a signed record in the node's published-record slot (sourced from the signing step, not a network read-back) and that its `RepublishManager` therefore schedules the 6-day relay arm rather than sitting at zero arms — the honest-absence dormancy asserted by `self_did_republishing_fully_dormant_without_published_record` (SCP-RELAYRES-004) must now apply only to a node that has genuinely published nothing on EITHER layer.

No misnomer left behind: `grep -rn 'publish_did_document_for_mode' crates/` returns 0 matches (including the doc-comment references in crates/scp-node/src/config.rs, crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs and crates/scp-node/tests/self_host.rs), and the replacement name does not imply DHT-only gating.

No implicit layer opt-out: a test asserts an explicit `RepublishConfig::disable_relay()` emits the §3.10.6 warning ("DID resolution layer disabled. This identity may not be resolvable by all peers."), and that no production code path disables either layer implicitly — `grep -rn 'disable_relay\|disable_dht' crates/scp-node/src` returns 0 matches.

Every `impl DidMethod` and every relay-leg call site carries a real value, no stubs: `cargo build --workspace` succeeds and `grep -rn 'todo!\|unimplemented!' crates/scp-identity/src crates/scp-node/src` returns 0 matches — the relay leg either publishes a real frame or returns a typed error, never a fabricated success.

Full CI green: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; the workspace clippy command; `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$(python3.12 -c "import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_config_var('LIBDIR'))") cargo test --workspace` — all exit 0.
`python3.12 scripts/validate-prd.py` exits 0 with this story present.
actionItems: Split the gating in the node publish path (crates/scp-node/src/lib.rs): sign unconditionally, keep the DHT leg gated on `DhtMode`, and gate the relay leg only on the relay layer's own enablement so a `DhtMode::Disabled` node still relay-publishes (§3.10.6). Do NOT re-derive the signed record — `DidMethod::publish` already returns it (delivered by SCP-RELAYRES-004).

Add the §3.10.5 step 3a relay leg inside the node's single publish seam: wrap the returned signed record in a `DidRecordV1` and PUBLISH it via the shared `TransportRelayPublisher` with `blob_ttl: 604800`, in parallel with the DHT leg, so both legs consume the one signing.

Rename the publish entry point so it names both layers instead of the DHT mode, and update every reference including the doc comments in crates/scp-node/src/config.rs, crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs and crates/scp-node/tests/self_host.rs.

Make the node's published-record slot receive the signed record on a `DhtMode::Disabled` create (today that path returns `Ok(None)`), so a Disabled node's `RepublishManager` schedules the 6-day relay arm instead of staying fully dormant.

Confirm the SDK capability matrix needs no new cell (this is a behaviour correction on an existing identity-publish surface, not a new operation) and record that check; write the both-legs-one-signing, Disabled-still-relay-publishes, Disabled-not-dormant, rename, and no-implicit-opt-out tests; run full CI + review roster.

details.delivered_by_004: Two acceptance criteria carried by an earlier revision of this story were delivered by SCP-RELAYRES-004 and have been REMOVED here so nobody re-implements them. (1) "The signed BEP44 record is an OUTPUT of signing, not a storage read-back" — `DidMethod::publish` now returns `Result<republish::RepublishEntry, IdentityError>` (crates/scp-identity/src/lib.rs, the `fn publish` trait method; the record is constructed at the end of `DidDht::publish_document` in crates/scp-identity/src/dht.rs). (2) "`self_did_republish_entry` no longer reconstructs the triple from a DHT read-back" — the function no longer exists (`grep -n 'self_did_republish_entry' crates/` returns 0) and `grep -n 'dht_client.resolve' crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs` returns 0; the republish cycle reads the node's published-record slot directly, covered by `republishing_survives_a_dht_read_back_miss_at_startup` (crates/scp-node/src/self_host.rs).
details.retracted_premise: That earlier revision stated as root cause that "`DidDht::publish_document` ... returns `Result<(), IdentityError>` — so no caller can build the `DidRecordV1` frame the relay leg needs" and that "`self_did_republish_entry` ... has to reconstruct the triple by resolving the node's own record back OFF THE DHT". Both statements are FALSE against current code and are retracted. The genuine remaining root cause is narrower: the node's publish path gates BOTH legs on `DhtMode`, so a `DhtMode::Disabled` node publishes nothing anywhere and has no signed record at all.
